prompt:
Render a high-fidelity desktop website homepage for VomerLabs, edge to edge at landscape aspect 16:10, with crisp readable UI text and no browser window, device, or desk around it. VomerLabs is an independent studio building software, exploring practical uses for AI, and sharing what is learned. Its visitors are potential software clients and fellow builders; they need to understand the studio, see honest real work, and contact its owner. The brief pins a calm, minimal editorial style, flat warm off-white #F5F3EE, near-black #171815, muted gray-green #8C9185, and soft lime #C6F277 used sparingly. Clean sans-serif text, with mono reserved for project metadata.
Use the real text “VomerLabs”, “Ideas into useful things.”, “VomerLabs is an independent studio where I build software, explore practical uses for AI, and share what I learn.” Navigation uses Work, Studio, Contact. The direct action is “Get in touch” with hi@vomerlabs.com. The only featured project is “VomerLabs website”, status “In progress”, description “A home for the studio, its projects, and the process behind them.” Its technical metadata is “Astro · Markdown · Plain CSS”. Include “About this build” as the project-detail anchor. There are no other projects or published lab notes, no clients, metrics, testimonials, or launch claims.
Make the page a living open index, not a software dashboard. One continuous reading surface: compact masthead, a large left-aligned typographic statement with the short introduction in its open margin, then a full-width open catalogue row for the website build visible in the same viewport. Let the project title and honest status be the evidence; do not invent a screenshot or use a generic illustrated hero. Distinguish studio introduction, project record, and contact through a deliberate typographic hierarchy and shared column edges. A section below begins with “Software, practical AI, and a thoughtful process.” Keep navigation and contact obviously clickable and the page calm but unmistakably authored. The whole first viewport must work as a real homepage, not a poster.
approvalSource: User selected working-index on decision page 4474f9e6, then confirmed in chat: I've already picked the first one
